_about:
Build supply_demand.json, the inputs of the supply-and-demand layer (supply_demand.py).

  python3 make_supply_demand.py <Single-Aisle_Replacement_Demand html>

Sources:
- Airbus supply: the user's chart "Airbus NGSA Production Assessment, A320 Program and NGSA Transition (Rev. B)",
  digitised here as (calendar year, aircraft a month) points: A320 final-assembly rate (base and Alt) and the NGSA
  rate, drawn for NGSA entry into service in mid-2037. The Alt plan keeps the A320 lines longer: "+~1,500 A320
  airplanes, +~$700-800M".
- Demand: the user's page "Single-Aisle Replacement Demand" (Cirium fleet data, 5 and 7 Oct 2026): replacements a
  year of today's 737 MAX, A320neo-family and A220 fleets, firm orders included, on the page's default schedule
  (delivery streams, historical pace, history start), and the split of those replacements by customer group.
- Boeing supply: 737 MAX path and site split from the research notes in supply_demand_sources.md.

airbus.alt_cost_note: midpoint of the chart's '+ ~$700-800M' for the Alt plan, booked in the NGSA entry-into-service year

demand.note: demand(y) = base_per_year + replacements(y); base set so 2026-2045 averages the board's 2,000 a year. flex_share: customers flying both types, lessors and unannounced customers, as a share of replacements over the flex window; they take the other maker's spare slots when their first choice cannot deliver; single-fleet customers wait (their unmet demand is lost to the year).
demand.lapse_note: a fifth of waiting customers give up each year (mean wait about five years, the page's 5-7 year lead time from commitment to first deliveries); the model starts in 2026 with no backlog: today's firm orders are part of the demand the factories already cannot meet

boeing._about: Boeing supply inputs, from the research notes (supply_demand_sources.md, October 2026).
boeing.max_rate_source: Research base path: 47 a month cleared 27 May 2026 but not stable (actual 2026 output about 42-43 a month); 52 about mid-2027 with the Everett North Line (opened July 2026); 57, Boeing's stated goal, about mid-2029; flat after. Bounds: MS 52 flat (low), 63 by 2030 (high, the four-line ceiling).
boeing.site_source: Renton: three final assembly lines, held at 47 a month (Boeing, July 2026); Everett North Line: about $1B, capacity about 15-16 a month (Leeham), takes the builds for 52 and beyond.
boeing.rate_increase_note: the board's 737 rate increase: +5 pp of its 2,000-aircraft market from 2032 = +100 aircraft a year (about 8 a month, to about 65: the four-line ceiling of 62-63 plus a second North Line)
boeing.renton_saving_source: Research estimate (2025$): new-site capex for about 50 a month at about $80M per unit of monthly rate = $4.0B, less about $1.0B to convert Renton = $3.0B central ($1.5B-$5.5B). Booked at fps entry into service, as the board books bills.
boeing.fps_ramp_note: fps capacity ramps on the NGSA chart's shape (rate 50 about 4 years after EIS, 100 about 8 years after), shifted to the fps EIS
